Context (previous page): η(ω) = q^{1/12}∏(1−q^{2ν}) with q = e^{πiω}, so ϑ1'(0,ω) = 2π η(ω)^3. For αδ−βγ = 1 and β ≠ 0, formula III there reads: log η((γ+δω)/(α+βω)) = log η(ω) + ½ log((α+βω)/(βi)) + ¼ log β² + kπi/12. The branch of the log has imaginary part in (−π/2, π/2), log β² is real, and k is an integer depending only on α,β,γ,δ. To determine k, let ω → −α/β with y → 0 and (α+βx)²/y → 0. Then ω' = δ/β − 1/(β(α+βω)) tends to i∞ in such a way that q' → 0, so log η(ω') − ω'πi/12 → 0.

This page.
(1) Substituting log η(ω') ≈ ω'πi/12 into III gives the 'Annäherungssatz': 0 = log η(ω) + ½ log((α+βω)/(βi)) + ¼ log β² + πi/(12β(α+βω)) + hπi/12 − δπi/(12β), with h = k.
(2) All terms except the last two depend only on α and β. Hence the integer hβ − α − δ =: (−α,β) depends only on the coprime pair (α,β). Writing α = −m, β = n gives formula II: 0 = log η(ω) + πi/(12n(nω−m)) + ½ log((nω−m)/(ni)) + ¼ log n² + ((m,n)−m)/(12n)·πi. This holds as ω → m/n in the admissible way, i.e. y → 0 and (nx−m)²/y → 0.
(3) Replacing (m,n) by (−m,−n) leaves the first three terms of II unchanged. Hence ((−m,−n)+m)/(−12n) = ((m,n)−m)/(12n), i.e. (III) (−m,−n) = −(m,n).
(4) From the definition, (−α,β) = hβ − α − δ ≡ −α−δ (mod β), and αδ ≡ 1 (mod β). With α = −m: (m,n) ≡ m − δ, where −mδ ≡ 1. Multiplying by m gives (IV) m(m,n) ≡ m² + 1 (mod n).
(5) Using kπi/12 = (hβ)πi/(12β) = ((−α,β)+α+δ)πi/(12β), the transformation formula becomes (I): log η((γ+δω)/(α+βω)) = log η(ω) + ½ log((α+βω)/(βi)) + ¼ log β² + ((−α,β)+α+δ)/(12β)·πi.
(6) Fundamental properties: η(ω+1) = e^{πi/12}η(ω), so log η(1+ω) = log η(ω) + πi/12. As ω → m/n, 1+ω → (m+n)/n, which is still in lowest terms, and n(1+ω) − (m+n) = nω − m. So II applied at (m+n)/n gives 0 = log η(1+ω) + πi/(12n(nω−m)) + ½ log((nω−m)/(ni)) + ¼ log n² + ((m+n,n)−m−n)/(12n)·πi. Comparing with II yields (next page, VI) (m+n,n) = (m,n).

In modern terms (my identification): (m,n) = 12 n s(m,n), where s is the Dedekind sum. Formula I is the standard η-multiplier formula: with the modern (a,b,c,d) = (δ,γ,β,α) and c > 0, the correction is πi(a+d)/(12c) − πi s(d,c). The next page derives the reciprocity law 12mn(s(m,n)+s(n,m)) = m²+n²+1−3mn. This is the text, essentially verbatim, of Dedekind's 'Erläuterungen' to Riemann's Fragment XXVIII in Riemann's Werke (1876).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is word-for-word the content of Dedekind's published commentary on Riemann's fragment on limiting values of modular functions (Riemann's Werke, 1876). The (m,n) symbol, the integer normalization and the reciprocity on the next page are what is credited to Dedekind. The style ('bekanntlich', the citation of Hermite 1858, the numbered theorems) suggests this is Dedekind's draft kept with the Riemann papers, not Riemann's own work. If it were genuinely Riemann's, it would be a major attribution shift. But as the material stands it is known and published, and the authorship is most likely Dedekind's.
